The payments sandbox rate-limits at 5 requests per second. This was the cause of test_payments flaking in CI.

**Why:** Integration tests that hit the sandbox in quick loops get throttled and fail at random.

**How to apply:** Any new test or script that calls the sandbox more than once should space calls at least 0.2s apart (tests/test_payments.py uses 0.25s via SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL). Also consider this first when sandbox-backed tests flake.

I added a 0.25-second pause after each sandbox call in `tests/test_payments.py`. I haven't run the test, since it needs the live sandbox.

- The pause length is stored in a constant, `SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL = 0.25`. A limit of 5 requests per second means calls must be at least 0.2s apart, so 0.25s leaves a little room for timing jitter.
- `test_charges_roundtrip` now calls `time.sleep(SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL)` after each POST, which adds about 1 second to the test.

If other test files call the sandbox, they could still exceed the limit when they run at the same time as this one, for example under `pytest-xdist`. A shared rate-limiting fixture would fix that if it's a problem.

I also saved the 5 requests per second limit to project memory so future sandbox-backed tests account for it.
